versos.texto_bv: Pode-se tomar o despojo de um guerreiro? Ou pode escapar o cativo de um justo?
versos.traducao_literal: Pode-se tomar do valente o despojo? E se do justo o cativo escapar?
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): Tradução de צַדִּיק (tsadiq) como "justo" diverge de ARA ("tirano"), NVIPT ("violentos") e NTLH ("rei cruel"); o paralelo poético com גִּבּוֹר (guerreiro/valente) sugere leitura de opressor poderoso, não de pessoa justa. — evidência: ARA: "Acaso tirar-se-ia a presa ao valente? ou serão libertados os cativos de um tirano?"; NVIPT: "do poder dos violentos"; NTLH: "por um rei cruel". A BV seguiu a glosa primária de צדק (justo), mas o contexto do paralelismo antitético pede leitura irônica ou negativa ("aquele que se considera justo"). Correção exigiria decisão exegética sobre o valor semântico contextual.

kjv.texto: Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered?

vizinhos.23: And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.
vizinhos.25: But thus saith the Lord, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.

web.texto: Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?

vizinhos.23: Kings shall be your nursing fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers: they shall bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet; and you shall know that I am Yahweh; and those who wait for me shall not be disappointed.”
vizinhos.25: But thus says Yahweh, “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the plunder of the terrible shall be delivered; for I will contend with him who contends with you, and I will save your children.

versos.texto_bv: E agora, diz o SENHOR — que me formou desde o ventre para ser seu servo, para trazer Jacó de volta a ele, e Israel não será reunido — serei honrado aos olhos do SENHOR, e meu Deus se tornou minha força.
versos.traducao_literal: E agora diz o SENHOR, o que me formou desde o ventre para servo a ele, para fazer voltar Jacó a ele, e Israel não é reunido — e serei honrado aos olhos do SENHOR, e o meu Deus tornou-se a minha força.
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): Divergência de sentido em "Israel não será reunido" (BV, seguindo leitura negativa literal do MT וְיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יֵאָסֵף) vs. "reunir Israel a ele" (ARA/NVIPT, leitura positiva). — evidência: ARA: "para tornar a trazer-lhe Jacó, e para reunir Israel a ele"; NVIPT: "para trazer de volta Jacó e reunir Israel a ele mesmo"; NTLH: "reunisse o seu povo e o trouxesse de volta". A BV seguiu a forma negativa do MT (לֹא יֵאָסֵף); as demais seguem leitura concessiva/positiva. Correção exigiria decisão exegética sobre a tradição textual.

kjv.texto: And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.

vizinhos.4: Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.
vizinhos.6: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.

web.texto: Now says Yahweh who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, and that Israel be gathered to him (for I am honorable in the eyes of Yahweh, and my God has become my strength);

vizinhos.4: But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely the justice due to me is with Yahweh, and my reward with my God.”
vizinhos.6: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
